identity.name: S CHAND AND COMPANY LTD
identity.industry: K-12 Educational Publishing & AI Content Licensing

summary.oneLiner: S Chand delivered strong FY26 results with 11% revenue growth and 18.1% EBITDA margin despite GST hike, driven by NCF adoption and 60%+ YoY AI licensing growth; FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reflects cost pressures from paper/logistics, but AI licensing (targeting Rs100cr in 3-5 years) and CPD Singapore acquisition create durable upside beyond traditional publishing.

one-line thesis: S Chand delivered strong FY26 results with 11% revenue growth and 18.1% EBITDA margin despite GST hike, driven by NCF adoption and 60%+ YoY AI licensing growth; FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reflects cost pressures from paper/logistics, but AI licensing (targeting Rs100cr in 3-5 years) and CPD Singapore acquisition create durable upside beyond traditional publishing.
financial scorecard: revenue: Rs8,000m (in-line with guidance); EBITDA: Rs1,449m (18.1% margin, met guidance); PAT (rptd): Rs731m (+21% YoY); PAT (normalized): Rs731m (no major one-offs); order book: N/A (publishing model); net debt: net cash Rs1,048m (debt-free)
guidance: revenue growth: 10%-15%; margin: 17%-19% (down 1pt due to paper/logistics inflation); order inflow: N/A; capex/commissioning: Rs20cr for new printing plant (Delhi), 100% in-house capacity target
segment / subsidiary detail: School Textbooks: NCF rollout complete by FY27; 1500+ schools adopted Milestone/My Zen/SmartK; Higher Ed: declining due to piracy (now 8% of revenue vs 20% pre-COVID); AI Licensing: Rs32cr FY25, target Rs40cr FY26, potential Rs100cr in 3-5 years; International: CPD Singapore acquired (Rs5cr revenue, profitable pre-acquisition), targeting 1000+ Indian schools + Middle East
growth verticals / optionality: AI licensing (10,000+ titles in repo, 30-40% licensed so far); CPD Singapore expansion into India/South Asia/Middle East; POD printing plant enabling lower inventory and smaller print runs
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin sustained at 68% despite 6% GST hike via product mix; EBITDA margin guidance lowered to 17-19% due to 10-15% paper price hike, fuel/logistics inflation, labor cost rise from new Labor Code; AI licensing margins ~90% on in-house content
capex / expansion: Rs20cr for new state-of-the-art printing plant near Delhi (to increase in-house capacity from 80-85% to near 100%); includes digital printing machines; Rs362cr total FY26 capex; Rs107cr for CPD acquisition
capital allocation: Net cash Rs1,048m; interim dividend Rs4/share maintained; buyback under consideration but deferred due to geopolitical uncertainty; M&A open for portfolio gaps (e.g., AI content, international curriculum); no debt repayment needed
risks & watch-items: Paper price volatility (10-15% hike expected); geopolitical disruption (Middle East collections delayed); higher education piracy; slow adoption of CPD in India; AI licensing client concentration risk; margin compression if price hikes capped at 6-8%
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term secular demand (K-8 books rebounding globally), pragmatic on cost pressures, cautious on buyback due to war uncertainty, optimistic on AI and international expansion
non-obvious takeaways: AI licensing revenue is not one-time-only — 70% is term-based (1-5 years), with 100% renewal rate; content reuse across clients is allowed (e.g., math books licensed to multiple LLMs); CPD’s revenue is from Singapore government schools (stable), not B2C; inventory days will normalize in 1HFY27 as NCF rollout completes
